Fixed the Fields of Fire phase display in [engine.py](api/app/core/engine.py). Starting the mission had updated the saved game phase, but the screen kept reading the stale generic phase index, making it look like nothing happened.

going back to the setup but this applies throughout the game.  there are stacking rules.  can you read through these rules and ensure that they are implimented.

5.1.5 Stacking
“Stacking” has two main meanings (beyond piling counters on
one another to keep things orderly):
1. Having more than one unit on a card.
• You may not have more than 16 steps and four vehicles per
side on a card at any time during a turn (see the note below
for possible exceptions).
• Steps embarked on vehicles do not count.
• Casualties do not count.
• Brewed up and wrecked vehicles do not count except when
using the card as a Landing Zone (see section 11).
• Staging Area cards do not have stacking limits.
2. Having more than one unit under a cover marker or in
an Urban Terrain building area.
• Some cover markers have a hard limit on how many steps
can fit in them. This is indicated on the counter (5.3.2).
• Except for the Out-of-Cover area and “outside” areas on Urban
Terrain cards, having more than 3 steps in a single area will
cause penalties when calculating combat effects (5.3).
Note: Certain situations outside of player control (Retreat,
arrival of preplanned amphibious invasion forces, Higher HQ
events, etc.) may result in a card becoming overstacked by
infantry units. If this is the case, you must move someone out
at the first opportunity to get back into limits.

data.content:
The card-level limits were already partly enforced: 16 steps and four vehicles per side, with staging-area, casualty, and embarked-unit exemptions. I fixed two gaps in [validator.py](api/app/games/fields_of_fire/validator.py): vehicle moves now check the destination’s vehicle limit, and wrecked/brewed-up vehicles count only on landing zones; destroyed vehicles do not count.

The rules are **not fully implemented yet**. The code does not currently model occupancy within cover-marker or urban building areas, marker-specific step capacities, or the combat penalty for more than three steps in an area. It also does not track the “move someone out at the first opportunity” exception for forced overstacking. I haven’t run tests.

## FoF Implementation Analysis Report

---

### **1. Frontend UI Controls & Capabilities by Phase**

**Setup Phase:**
- **Control:** Click on staging-area cards (deployment zones or `DZ_*` cards) to open placement popup
- **UI Elements:** 
  - Setup status panel showing "X/Y units placed"
  - "Start Mission" button (enabled when all required units placed and map has cards)
  - Unit selection popup with thumbnails for staging placement
- **What happens:** `handleCardClick` → opens popup; selecting unit calls `dispatch('select-move')` via backend placement validation

**Non-Setup Phases (friendly_higher_hq_event, friendly_command, enemy_activity, mutual_capture_retreat, at_combat_vehicle_movement, mutual_combat, clean_up):**
- **Control Mechanism:** Only moves in `legalMoves` from backend can be dispatched
  - `handleCardClick` → finds first legal move matching card position → dispatches it
  - Frontend has **no hardcoded phase checks** for gameplay phases; entirely reliant on backend `legalMoves`
- **Button for Confirm:** "Confirm" button appears when `confirmRequired === true` or `pendingMove !== null` (see [GameProgressPanel.svelte](web/src/lib/components/GameProgressPanel.svelte#L107-L111))
- **No "Next Phase" button** — phase transitions are implicit from move responses

**Display/Rendering:**
- **Rendered:** Friendly units (counters on map), stack hover previews, card images, terrain elevation (`?E`), cover ratings (`C`), markers count, VOF markers count
- **Missing/Not Rendered:**
  - Enemy units (not visible on board; only backend `gd.enemy[]` exists)
  - Individual marker details (only count displayed: "Markers: N | VOF: M")
  - Command pool/ammo/casualty counters
  - HQ activation UI
  - Command spending UI
  - Dice rolling UI
  - Fire resolution UI
  - Marker types displayed (fire_mission, grenade, sniper, flamethrower, etc. created but not shown visually)

**Move Confirmation Flow:**
- If `confirm_required === false` (default for most phases): move auto-submits
- If `confirm_required === true`: move stageable in `pendingMove`, "Confirm" button shows
- `handleConfirm()` → calls `makeMove()` on pending, then optionally `confirmTurn()` if phase still requires confirm

**Setup Phase:**

**Gameplay Phases:**
- **No phase checks in UI.** Backend `legalMoves` is the single source of truth.
- Each clickable action finds a move via `getLegalMoveForCard()` → `legalMoves.find(m => m.type === ... && m.position === idx)`
- If no legal move exists for a position, card click does nothing
- Confirm button enabled only when `confirmRequired === true` OR `pendingMove !== null`

data.content:
## Plan: Fields of Fire rules enforcement for Normandy Mission 1

Most of the rules are not enforced yet. Setup and stacking are mostly in place, but after setup the game is a skeleton. The plan below builds the missing foundations first, then the rules, then the UI, with playable checkpoints along the way.

### Where we are now

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Setup placement (staging area only), setup completeness | Enforced |
| Stacking: 16 steps and 4 vehicles per side per card, with the 5.1.5 exemptions | Enforced for infantry and vehicles, including `move_vehicle` |
| Stacking: cover-marker capacity, urban areas, more than 3 steps penalty, forced overstack | Missing |
| Movement cost (1 command per card) | Deducted in `apply_move` but never validated against the pool |
| Command rules (HQ activation order, chain of command, communication, command range) | Missing |
| Fire, rally, fire missions, mines, embark/disembark, buildings, helicopters | Stubs that only append an unresolved marker |
| Combat and enemy helpers (`resolve_fire`, `has_los`, enemy activity check and others) | Written but never called |
| Phase sequence | `advance_phase` accepts any phase name; no automatic phase effects |
| Action Deck / randomness | Missing |
| UI after setup | No Next Phase, Activate HQ, Draw Commands, command pool, enemy units or marker detail |

- **Action Deck:** the rules run on a 50-card Action Deck plus a reshuffle card, not dice. Commands, activity checks, combat results, Potential Contact and random numbers all come from it. The card images exist in `documentation/fof/organized/Cards/Action Cards Draw/`, but there is no structured card data. This blocks almost everything else.
- **Fake legal moves:** `get_legal_moves` offers placeholder moves such as position 0 or `m113_1`.
- **Validator bugs:** unreachable `return` in the `place_enemy` check; `place_vehicle` and `place_unit` can append duplicates; `enemy_activity_check` burns mortar ammo; `open_fire` adds a duplicate VOF marker.
- **Tests:** there is no Playwright config, though `@playwright/test` is installed. The extended FoF tests mostly assert trivial placeholders. `test_setup_card_click_can_create_new_stack_outside_legacy_deployment_zones` now contradicts the staging-only rule.

### Steps

**Phase 0 – Baseline (fast, unblocks the rest)**
1. Fix the validator bugs above.
2. Replace placeholder legal moves with moves generated from real state.
3. Make `advance_phase` follow the 3.1–3.8 order.
4. Update the stale test to expect rejection, and re-run the isolated FoF test files.

**Phase 1 – Foundations** *(depends on 0)*
1. Transcribe the 50 Action cards (A01–A50 plus the reshuffle card) into a new `api/configs/fof/action_deck.json`. Per card: activated and initiative commands, action icons, HQ event, AT number, the Combat Resolution column (−4 to +6 → HIT/PIN/MISS), hit effect by Vet/Line/Green, and the random-number row. Add deck-level validation and a review pass, since transcription accuracy matters.
2. Add deck state in `game_data`:
   - seeded shuffle, draw pile and discard;
   - the "draw the full count, then reshuffle" rule;
   - a visible draw/roll log;
   - injectable draws for tests.
3. Make the turn sequence server-driven: 3.1 Higher HQ Event (from Turn 2), 3.3 Command with its impulses, 3.4 Enemy Activity, 3.5 Capture & Retreat, 3.6 AT & Vehicle, 3.7 Combat segments, 3.8 Clean Up. Automatic steps run and log; the player is only prompted for decisions.

**Phase 2 – Command, control and movement (3.3, 4.1–4.3, 5.1)** *(depends on 1)*
1. Activation segment: BN HQ is off-map in Normandy, so the CO HQ is activated. Commands come from an Action card draw, with the 4.1.2 modifiers and the 4.1.3 per-turn limits by visibility and experience.
2. PLT HQ and CO Staff impulses, then the Initiative segment; general initiative commands cannot be saved.
3. Orders must respect chain of command and communication (starting with visual-verbal and the SCR-536 radio).
4. Validate spending against the command pool. Movement needs orthogonal adjacency and terrain costs, and applies Activated and Moved/Fired markers. Use one source of truth for movement cost.

**Phase 3 – Stacking completion and cover (5.1.5, 5.3)** *(depends on 2)*
1. Cover markers: placement and counter-specified step capacity.
2. Urban buildings and "outside" areas.
3. The more-than-3-steps penalty, exposed to combat as a modifier.
4. Forced-overstack tracking from retreat, arrivals and Higher HQ events; the card must be cleared at the first opportunity.

**Phase 4 – Combat (6.x, 7.x, 10.x as Mission 1 needs)** *(depends on 1 and 2)*
1. VOF and PDF markers, LOS, range bands, engagement priorities.
2. Net combat modifier, then the Action card HIT/PIN/MISS result and hit effects. Add casualties, pinned, rally and ammo.
3. Mortar and artillery fire missions; AT fire.
4. Wire in the helpers that are kept and delete the dead ones.

**Phase 5 – Enemy system (8.x)** *(depends on 4)*
1. Potential Contact A/B/C by row and the Potential Contact Draw Chart.
2. Enemy package placement for the Mission 1 catalog.
3. Activity checks for deliberate defense, fire/shift/cease fire, fall back, spotters, snipers and mines.
4. Higher HQ event tables, and capture and retreat.

**Phase 6 – Mission 1 completion** *(depends on 5)*
1. 3.8 clean-up.
2. Victory: secure both objectives and clear Rows 1–2, with limit of advance and the 10-turn cap.
3. The `counter_attack` special rule, and experience award.

**Phase 7 – UI** *(starts after Phase 1, parallel with 2–6)*
1. Action panel: phase and segment, Continue, Activate HQ, command pool per HQ, orders menu on a selected stack, and a roll/draw log.
2. Enemy and marker layers, stacking warnings, combat results.
3. Drive everything from backend legal moves, replacing the "click card → first legal move" behaviour.
4. Split the large `FieldsOfFireBoard.svelte` into sub-components.

**Phase 8 – Verification** *(continuous)*
1. Per-rule pytest files organized by rulebook section number.
2. Seeded scenario replays.
3. A Playwright smoke test (the dependency is already installed).
4. Isolated test runs only, per your repo guardrails.

### Playable checkpoints

1. **After Phases 0–2:** turn loop, HQ activation, command-limited movement and stacking.
2. **After 3–4:** firefights.
3. **After 5:** enemy contact.
4. **After 6:** the full Mission 1.

### Relevant files
- `api/app/games/fields_of_fire/validator.py`: validation, legal moves and `apply_move`; `_stack_*` helpers.
- `api/app/core/engine.py`: phase sync (`get_phase_info`, `_sync_validator_transition`).
- `api/configs/fof/fields_of_fire_scenarios.json`: `normandy_mission_1`.
- `api/configs/fof/fields_of_fire.yaml`: phase config.
- `documentation/fof/README.md`: rule text and charts.
- `web/src/lib/components/games/fields_of_fire/FieldsOfFireBoard.svelte` and `web/src/routes/games/[gameId]/play/+page.svelte`.
- `api/tests/test_fields_of_fire.py` and `api/tests/test_fields_of_fire_extended.py`.

### Decisions
- Scope is the full Normandy Mission 1, driven through a phase/action control panel.
- Randomness is seeded server-side with a visible log and test injection.
- Stacking leftovers are built in alongside the core rules.
- Mechanics Mission 1 doesn't use (helicopters, amphibious assault, Vietnam/Korea tables) stay deferred.

### Further considerations
1. **Action card transcription:** I can read each card image and extract the data myself, then validate it with deck-level checks. The alternative is you confirming a sample. I recommend I transcribe, and you spot-check about 10 cards.
2. **Phase 0 timing:** it's small and unblocks everything, so I'd do it first, in one pass.

{"filePath": "c:\Users\p211587\personal\dev\rbgg\api\app\games\fields_of_fire\action_deck.py", "content": """"Fields of Fire Action Deck mechanics (rulebook 1.2.2, 1.2.7, 2.2.3).

The deck is 50 Action cards (A01-A50) plus one reshuffle card. Hint cards are
not part of the deck. All state is plain JSON-serialisable dicts so it can be
stored in ``game_data``.

Rules implemented here:
- A draw always takes the full requested number of cards, even if a result
  is reached earlier (2.2.3).
- If the reshuffle card is reached during a draw, the draw is completed and
  then every card (including the reshuffle card) is reshuffled. The reshuffle
  card does not count as one of the required draws.

Randomness is seeded so games are reproducible. Tests and debugging may force
the next draws with ``force_next``; forced cards are still logged.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import random
from typing import Any

RESHUFFLE_CARD = "RESHUFFLE"
ACTION_CARD_IDS = [f"A{i:02d}" for i in range(1, 51)]


def new_action_deck(seed: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a freshly shuffled Action Deck state."""
    deck: dict[str, Any] = {
        "seed": seed,
        "shuffle_count": 0,
        "draw_pile": list(ACTION_CARD_IDS) + [RESHUFFLE_CARD],
        "discard": [],
        "forced": [],
        "log": [],
    }
    _shuffle(deck)
    return deck


def _shuffle(deck: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    cards = deck["draw_pile"] + deck["discard"]
    deck["discard"] = []
    rng = random.Random(f"{deck['seed']}:{deck['shuffle_count']}")
    rng.shuffle(cards)
    deck["draw_pile"] = cards
    deck["shuffle_count"] += 1


def force_next(deck: dict[str, Any], card_ids: list[str]) -> None:
    """Queue card ids to be drawn next, in order. For tests and debugging."""
    for card_id in card_ids:
        if card_id != RESHUFFLE_CARD and card_id not in ACTION_CARD_IDS:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown action card: {card_id}")
    deck["forced"].extend(card_ids)


def draw(deck: dict[str, Any], count: int, reason: str = "") -> list[str]:
    """Draw ``count`` Action cards, applying the reshuffle rule.

    Returns the drawn card ids (never the reshuffle card). Every draw is
    appended to ``deck["log"]``.
    """
    if count < 1:
        raise ValueError("count must be at least 1")
    drawn: list[str] = []
    reshuffle_pending = False
    while len(drawn) < count:
        card = _take_top(deck)
        if card == RESHUFFLE_CARD:
            reshuffle_pending = True
            continue
        drawn.append(card)
        deck["discard"].append(card)
    if reshuffle_pending:
        # Reshuffle only after the required draws are complete.
        deck["discard"].append(RESHUFFLE_CARD)
        _shuffle(deck)
    deck["log"].append({"reason": reason, "cards": list(drawn), "reshuffled": reshuffle_pending})
    return drawn


def _take_top(deck: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    if deck["forced"]:
        forced = deck["forced"].pop(0)
        if forced in deck["draw_pile"]:
            deck["draw_pile"].remove(forced)
        elif forced in deck["discard"]:
            deck["discard"].remove(forced)
        return forced
    if not deck["draw_pile"]:
        _shuffle(deck)
    return deck["draw_pile"].pop(0)
"}

    deck["draw_pile"] = cards
    deck["shuffle_count"] += 1


def force_next(deck: dict[str, Any], card_ids: list[str]) -> None:
    """Queue card ids to be drawn next, in order. For tests and debugging."""
    for card_id in card_ids:
        if card_id != RESHUFFLE_CARD and card_id not in ACTION_CARD_IDS:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown action card: {card_id}")
    deck["forced"].extend(card_ids)


def draw(deck: dict[str, Any], count: int, reason: str = "") -> list[str]:
    """Draw ``count`` Action cards, applying the reshuffle rule.

    Returns the drawn card ids (never the reshuffle card). Every draw is
    appended to ``deck["log"]``.
    """
    if count < 1:
        raise ValueError("count must be at least 1")
    drawn: list[str] = []
    reshuffle_pending = False
    while len(drawn) < count:
        card = _take_top(deck)
        if card == RESHUFFLE_CARD:
            reshuffle_pending = True
            continue
        drawn.append(card)
        deck["discard"].append(card)
    if reshuffle_pending:
        # Reshuffle only after the required draws are complete.
        deck["discard"].append(RESHUFFLE_CARD)
        _shuffle(deck)
    deck["log"].append({"reason": reason, "cards": list(drawn), "reshuffled": reshuffle_pending})
    return drawn


def _take_top(deck: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    if deck["forced"]:
        forced = deck["forced"].pop(0)
        if forced in deck["draw_pile"]:
            deck["draw_pile"].remove(forced)
        elif forced in deck["discard"]:
            deck["discard"].remove(forced)
        return forced
    if not deck["draw_pile"]:
        _shuffle(deck)
    return deck["draw_pile"].pop(0)

{"content": """"Combat Resolution lookup (rulebook 2.8.3, 6.4.2).

Each Action card carries a Combat Resolution column: net modifiers from -4 to
+6, each mapped to HIT, PIN or MISS. Given the net modifier (Volume of Fire
plus Cover & Concealment and other conditions), this returns the result.

This is read-only: it does not resolve fire, place markers or change state.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

RESULTS = ("HIT", "PIN", "MISS")
MIN_MODIFIER = -4
MAX_MODIFIER = 6
_PAIR = re.compile(r"([+-]?\d+)\s+(HIT|PIN|MISS)")


def parse_combat_resolution(text: str) -> dict[int, str]:
    """Parse a combat_resolution string into {modifier: result}.

    Raises ValueError if the column is malformed or does not cover every
    modifier from -4 to +6 exactly once.
    """
    table: dict[int, str] = {}
    for part in (text or "").split(";"):
        part = part.strip()
        if not part:
            continue
        match = _PAIR.fullmatch(part)
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"malformed combat resolution entry: {part!r}")
        modifier = int(match.group(1))
        if modifier in table:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate combat resolution modifier: {modifier}")
        table[modifier] = match.group(2)
    expected = set(range(MIN_MODIFIER, MAX_MODIFIER + 1))
    if set(table) != expected:
        raise ValueError(f"combat resolution must cover {MIN_MODIFIER} to {MAX_MODIFIER}")
    return table


def resolve_combat(text: str, net_modifier: int) -> str:
    """Return HIT, PIN or MISS for a net modifier on a card's resolution column.

    Modifiers beyond -4 or +6 use the nearest printed value, since the column
    only prints that range.
    """
    table = parse_combat_resolution(text)
    clamped = max(MIN_MODIFIER, min(MAX_MODIFIER, int(net_modifier)))
    return table[clamped]

A VOF marker records the fire affecting a card. Each rating has a value; the
lower (better) value is the one that applies to a unit (6.2: "The best VOF

from typing import Any

# 6.2.2 Basic VOF ratings and the value of the marker they place.
VOF_VALUES: dict[str, int] = {"S": 0, "A": -1, "H": -3, "PINNED": 2}
# A/S places an Automatic (-1) marker at point blank and a Small Arms (0)
# marker at any other range.
AS_POINT_BLANK = -1
AS_OTHER = 0
SUPPORTED_RATINGS = tuple(VOF_VALUES) + ("A/S",)


def vof_value(rating: str, point_blank: bool = False) -> int:
    """Return the marker value for a rating. Raises ValueError if unsupported."""
    if rating == "A/S":
        return AS_POINT_BLANK if point_blank else AS_OTHER
    if rating in VOF_VALUES:
        return VOF_VALUES[rating]
    raise ValueError(f"unsupported VOF rating: {rating!r}")

    """Return the best (lowest value) VOF marker on a card, or None.

    Only markers placed on the card itself are considered. Each marker is
    compared by its stored ``value``.
    """
    on_card = [
        m for m in markers
        if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("position") == position and isinstance(m.get("value"), int)
    ]
    if not on_card:
        return None
    return min(on_card, key=lambda m: m["value"])

def test_unsupported_rating_has_no_value():

        vof_value("G!")

    move = {"type": "place_vof", "position": 4, "rating": "H"}

{"content": """"Primary Direction of Fire (PDF) rules (rulebook 6.3).

A PDF marker sits on the edge of the firing card and points toward a target
card. It is placed when a unit exerts a Basic VOF (S, A, H or Pinned) at a
card other than its own (6.3.1).

Cards are laid out on a grid of ``cols`` columns with index = row * cols + col,
where row 0 is the bottom row of the map as used by the board (the same
convention as the rest of the Fields of Fire board code).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

COMPASS = {
    "N": (1, 0),
    "S": (-1, 0),
    "E": (0, 1),
    "W": (0, -1),
}


def target_card(position: int, direction: str, rows: int, cols: int) -> int | None:
    """Return the card index a PDF points at, or None if it leaves the map."""
    if direction not in COMPASS:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported PDF direction: {direction!r}")
    if rows <= 0 or cols <= 0 or not 0 <= position < rows * cols:
        return None
    row, col = divmod(position, cols)
    d_row, d_col = COMPASS[direction]
    new_row, new_col = row + d_row, col + d_col
    if not (0 <= new_row < rows and 0 <= new_col < cols):
        return None
    return new_row * cols + new_col

{"content": """"Line of Sight between board cards (rulebook 5.2.1).

LOS is traced along the eight straight directions only. Adjacent cards are
always in LOS. Beyond that, each card the line passes through must have white
borders on both the entry and exit sides. Dark and black borders block LOS.

Border order matches the terrain loader and cards-final.json: a card's
``borders`` list is [north, east, south, west].

Range is at most three cards (Very Long Range), or one card (Close Range) in
limited visibility (9.1).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable

# Eight straight directions: (row delta, col delta).
DIRECTIONS = {
    "N": (1, 0),
    "NE": (1, 1),
    "E": (0, 1),
    "SE": (-1, 1),
    "S": (-1, 0),
    "SW": (-1, -1),
    "W": (0, -1),
    "NW": (1, -1),
}
# Border index for the side a line leaves through and enters through.
_BORDER_INDEX = {"N": 0, "E": 1, "S": 2, "W": 3}
# Edges a diagonal line exits/enters. Diagonals cross a corner, so both
# adjacent edges must be white.
_DIAGONAL_EDGES = {
    "NE": ("N", "E"),
    "SE": ("S", "E"),
    "SW": ("S", "W"),
    "NW": ("N", "W"),
}
MAX_RANGE = 3
MAX_RANGE_LIMITED = 1


def _edges_for(direction: str, leaving: bool) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Edges of a card a straight or diagonal line touches when crossing it."""
    if direction in _DIAGONAL_EDGES:
        return _DIAGONAL_EDGES[direction]
    # Straight line: leaving a card goes out the side in the direction of travel;
    # entering the next card comes in from the opposite side.
    edge = direction
    if leaving:
        return (edge,)
    opposite = {"N": "S", "S": "N", "E": "W", "W": "E"}[edge]
    return (opposite,)


def _cell(position: int, rows: int, cols: int, delta: tuple[int, int], steps: int) -> int | None:
    row, col = divmod(position, cols)
    new_row = row + delta[0] * steps
    new_col = col + delta[1] * steps
    if not (0 <= new_row < rows and 0 <= new_col < cols):
        return None
    return new_row * cols + new_col


def los_path(origin: int, target: int, rows: int, cols: int) -> list[int] | None:
    """Return the cards on the straight line from origin to target, or None.

    The result includes origin and target. None means the target is not on
    one of the eight straight lines from origin.
    """
    if origin == target:
        return [origin]
    if not (0 <= origin < rows * cols and 0 <= target < rows * cols):
        return None
    o_row, o_col = divmod(origin, cols)
    t_row, t_col = divmod(target, cols)
    d_row, d_col = t_row - o_row, t_col - o_col
    steps = max(abs(d_row), abs(d_col))
    if steps == 0:
        return [origin]
    # Must be exactly a straight or diagonal line.
    if d_row not in (0, steps, -steps) or d_col not in (0, steps, -steps):
        return None
    if d_row and d_col and abs(d_row) != abs(d_col):
        return None
    unit = (
        (d_row // steps) if d_row else 0,
        (d_col // steps) if d_col else 0,
    )
    return [_cell(origin, rows, cols, unit, k) for k in range(steps + 1)]


def has_los(
    origin: int,
    target: int,
    rows: int,
    cols: int,
    borders: Callable[[int], list[str]],
    limited: bool = False,
) -> bool:
    """True if target is in line of sight from origin under rulebook 5.2.1.

    ``borders(position)`` returns the four border colours of a card, in
    [north, east, south, west] order. Missing cards count as blocked.
    """
    path = los_path(origin, target, rows, cols)
    if path is None:
        return False
    distance = len(path) - 1
    if distance == 0:
        return True
    max_range = MAX_RANGE_LIMITED if limited else MAX_RANGE
    if distance > max_range:
        return False
    # Adjacent cards are always in LOS.
    if distance == 1:
        return True
    direction = _direction_between(origin, path[1], rows, cols)
    # Each intermediate card must pass the line from entry to exit side, and the
    # origin card must let the line leave. The target card only needs its entry side.
    for index, card in enumerate(path[1:-1], start=1):
        colours = borders(card)
        entry = _edges_for(direction, leaving=False)
        exit_ = _edges_for(direction, leaving=True)
        if any(colours[_BORDER_INDEX[edge]] != "white" for edge in entry + exit_):
            return False
    origin_colours = borders(origin)
    if any(origin_colours[_BORDER_INDEX[edge]] != "white" for edge in _edges_for(direction, leaving=True)):
        return False
    target_colours = borders(target)
    if any(target_colours[_BORDER_INDEX[edge]] != "white" for edge in _edges_for(direction, leaving=False)):
        return False
    return True


def _direction_between(a: int, b: int, rows: int, cols: int) -> str:
    a_row, a_col = divmod(a, cols)
    b_row, b_col = divmod(b, cols)
    d = (
        (b_row - a_row) and ((b_row - a_row) // abs(b_row - a_row)),
        (b_col - a_col) and ((b_col - a_col) // abs(b_col - a_col)),
    )
    for name, delta in DIRECTIONS.items():
        if delta == (d[0] or 0, d[1] or 0):
            return name
    raise ValueError("cards are not adjacent along a straight line")

**What it does** ([los.py](api/app/games/fields_of_fire/los.py))
- **Straight lines only:** a target is in LOS only if it sits on one of the eight straight directions from the origin. Knight-style and off-line targets are rejected.
- **Adjacent cards:** always in LOS, whatever the borders.
- **Longer range:** each card the line crosses must have white borders on both the entry and exit sides. A dark or black border blocks it.
- **Range limits:** three cards maximum, or one card under limited visibility.

**Checks I made**
- Border order (north, east, south, west) matches the terrain loader and `cards-final.json`. I checked it against hedgerow N27: north and south are dark, east and west are white.

- **Elevation** (5.2.2) isn't modelled. The rulebook's LOS notes say elevation doesn't extend range, but it can still matter for what a unit sees.
- **Smoke, Incoming! and Air Strike!** (5.4) aren't modelled. Those cards block LOS out of the card.
- **The old `has_los` stub** in the validator is still there. It isn't called by the game, and I've left it alone rather than make a large unrelated change.

def _state(vof_markers=None, units=None):

    gd["map"]["rows"] = 1
    gd["map"]["cols"] = 3
    gd["vof_markers"] = list(vof_markers or [])
    gd["company"]["units"] = list(units or [])
    return v, {"game_data": gd}


def test_fire_is_not_offered_without_a_vof_marker():
    v, state = _state()
    fires = [m for m in v.get_legal_moves(state, "p1") if m["type"] == "fire"]
    assert fires == []


def test_fire_is_offered_on_a_card_with_a_vof_marker():
    v, state = _state(vof_markers=[{"position": 1, "value": -1}])
    fires = [m for m in v.get_legal_moves(state, "p1") if m["type"] == "fire"]

    v, state = _state(vof_markers=[{"position": 1, "value": -1}])

def test_fire_records_a_result_from_the_drawn_card():

    assert record["net_modifier"] == -3
